title: Micro-ask plays and risk-led actions
summary: Rapid synthesis of high-frequency small asks from Q1 enterprise pilots and a prioritized set of mitigation plays by risk impact (customer-facing outage risk, cost-surprise, security/compliance). This is intentionally compact — meant to drive a 30-minute ops sync and a scoped engineering spike.
raw_notes:
Top signals observed across 12 pilot accounts (April check-ins):
- Confusion on per-route vs per-model billing; customers unexpectedly hit reserve compute when routing fallbacks triggered (3 accounts).
- Need ability to pin both model AND quantization profile for a route; teams are manually versioning and routing with brittle infra (5 accounts).
- Error surface: transient KV-cache evictions cause tail-latency spikes on long-history chat sessions; observed when autoscaler adds new workers (2 accounts, high severity).
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution unclear for reranks and streaming responses — support requests require manual repro and transcript stitching.
- Rollout friction: canary policy lacks traffic slice controls by user cohort; customers resort to duplicate endpoints.

Quotes/snippets from customers: 
- "We love the throughput but the bill was a surprise after a high-traffic day when fallbacks hit." — SRE lead, fintech pilot
- "We can't depend on autoscaling if it increases tail latency; need a safer warm-up plan." — ML infra eng, healthcare

Context notes: many asks are low-effort product changes or docs clarifications; a few are real infra risks requiring design spikes. Prioritization below tries to separate surface-level wins from systemic fixes.
prioritized_requests:
1) Billing clarity for mixed routing (high impact, mid effort)
- Ask: surface an exploded per-request cost breakdown (route, model-variant, fallback) in Console logs and API response header.
- Why: reduces billing surprise and support load.

2) Route-level pinned inference profile (medium impact, low effort)
- Ask: allow pinning (model-version + quantization-profile + runtime-flags) on a per-route basis.
- Why: customers can test quantization/latency combos without ad-hoc infra.

3) Safe autoscale warm-up hook (high impact, high effort)
- Ask: implement a warm-up handshake so new workers pre-load KV-caches for active conversations; optional pre-warm API for customers.
- Why: mitigates tail-latency regressions in long-dialogue apps.

4) Canary-by-cohort control (medium impact, medium effort)
- Ask: traffic slicing by identity label + weighted rollouts + rollback metrics.

5) Token-level tracing for streaming and rerank (high impact, mid effort)
- Ask: attach token attribution metadata to traces and Console Cost tab; make retracing for support reproducible.
proposed_quick_wins:
- Console: add a short explainer banner (under billing) about fallback routing costs + link to best practices (docs). Estimated: 1 frontend sprint.
- Docs: quick-runbook for ‘interpreting a surprise bill’ that support can use verbatim.
- API: add optional response header X-Redwood-Cost-Breakdown that clients can enable per-key. Small backend flag + header formatting.
- Rollout: add a UI toggle to pin quantization profile for a route (flags-only behind feature flag).
open_questions:
- For the warm-up hook: should warm-up be opt-in per-route or automatic with a budget cap?
- How to attribute cost for transient fallback invocations: charge origin route, serving route, or split?
- Security/compliance: will exposing per-token attribution metadata raise PII concerns for regulated customers? need legal input.
- What SLA/backpressure behavior do customers prefer when autoscaling is constrained? (reject, queue, or best-effort degrade)
next_steps:
1) Ops sync (30m) with ENG-serving-runtime + product-hosted-api: April 19 — decide quick-win scope and identify engineer owners (Diego/Evan).
2) Spike: warm-up design (2w): prototype pre-warm handshake + load test on long-history sessions (Maya assigned).
3) Docs + console UX: implement banner + support runbook (1 sprint).
4) Legal review request for token tracing, create ticket CS-4821, attach sample traces.
5) Weekly check-ins: publish one-line status updates to #cs-product and update Confluence page linked above.
final_notes: This doc is a compact playbook — treat as living. If any of the quick wins get blocked for >1 week, escalate to Head of Product for prioritization. We'll capture pilot customer feedback post-deploy and re-run impact estimate.
